question: Which of the following movements was NOT lead by Mahatma Gandhi?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bardoli Satyagraha, 1928**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bardoli Satyagraha (1928)
 
 
• The British government had imposed a significant increase in land revenue on farmers in Bardoli, Gujarat.
 
• This led to widespread discontent among the farmers.
 
• The Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928 was led by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
 
• Although Mahatma Gandhi provided support and strategic guidance, the direct leadership of the movement was under Patel. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Kheda Satyagraha (1918)
 
 
• A severe famine struck the Kheda district of Gujarat, leading to crop failures and widespread poverty.
 
• The British government refused to provide any relief to the affected farmers.
 
• Gandhi arrived in Kheda to assess the situation and galvanise the farmers into action.
 
• He encouraged them to refuse to pay taxes until they received adequate relief.
 
• The Kheda Satyagraha was another victory for Gandhi.
 
• The British government was forced to grant tax relief to the farmers, demonstrating the power of non-violent resistance.
 
 
 
• Passive Resistance Campaigns (1906)
 
 
• The British government had introduced discriminatory laws against Indian immigrants in South Africa, particularly the Transvaal.
 
• These laws limited the rights of Indians and subjected them to racial segregation.
 
• Gandhi led a series of passive resistance campaigns against these discriminatory laws.
 
• He encouraged Indians to refuse to obey unjust laws and to suffer the consequences peacefully.
 
• While the passive resistance campaigns in South Africa did not immediately achieve their goals, they helped to raise awareness of the plight of Indians and laid the foundation for Gandhi's later struggles for independence in India​
 
 
 
• Quit India Movement, 1942:
 
• Mahatma Gandhi Led this movement
 
 
• The Quit India Movement was a significant mass movement launched by Mahatma Gandhi on August 8, 1942, during World War II.
 
• The primary goal was to demand an end to British rule in India. Gandhi gave the famous "Do or Die" speech in Mumbai (then Bombay), urging Indians to do everything possible, non-violently, to drive the British out of India.
 
• The movement saw widespread civil disobedience and protests, with major impacts including the arrest of Gandhi and other leaders, violent suppression by the British, and a surge in nationalist sentiment among Indians.
